newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish businessmen predict '96 PSBR at 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkish businessmen predict '96 PSBR at 11 pct.

text.p: Turkish businessmen expect a sharp increase in Turkey's public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) this year and urge the government to take urgent measures to tackle chronic economic problems.

"The budget deficit and PSBR are anticipated at about nine percent and 11 percent of the gross national product (GNP)," Turkish Industrialists' and Businessmen's Association (TUSIAD) said in a report, obtained by Reuters on Friday.
The PSBR was 6.5 percent of the GNP in 1995.

TUSIAD, an influential lobbying group, said annual average inflation was expected to slow down to 80.5 percent this year from 88.5 percent in 1995 and the GNP growth rate to eight percent from 8.1 percent last year.
"Subsequently the foreign trade deficit is likely to exceed $19 billion, while the current account deficit could reach $6.7 billion," it said.
Foreign trade deficit stood at $14 billion and current account deficit at $2.3 billion last year.
"Timely and adequate solution to the chronic economic problems of the Turkish economy are needed to avoid undesirable economic disturbances," TUSIAD said.
It urged the government to take following steps:

"To make the finances of the public sector transparent, to impose mandatory economic constraints on the government such as upper limits on budget defcits, to discipline the financing of the public sector deficits, to introduce three-year budgets, to make the central bank autonomous, to deepen the financial system, to make a tax reform...to redress the social security system...to speed up privatisation..."
